issues.description: WriterLock.acquire() performs a genuine TOCTOU (time-of-check-to-time-of-use) race: exists()/is_live() check, then a decision, then an unconditional plain-text write (no O_CREAT|O_EXCL, no atomic rename) -- allowing multiple concurrent agents to all believe they hold exclusive write ownership simultaneously. A second, related bug: a stale (expired-lease) owner's own in-memory WriterLock object can later call .heartbeat() or .release() and unconditionally overwrite a DIFFERENT agent's legitimately-reclaimed lock, because neither method re-validates lock_id/ownership against what is actually currently on disk before writing -- .release()'s owned_by() check only compares against the stale caller's own remembered owner field, never re-reading the live file.

Only FileNotFoundError was caught (lines 133-136); JSONDecodeError (a ValueError) propagated out of acquire() -> the multiprocessing worker (_writer_lock_mp_worker.py:41-42) reported 'error' -> tests/unit/test_writer_lock_concurrency.py:78 'assert not errors' failed on Linux CI with JSONDecodeError('Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)'). Fix: in acquire()'s FileExistsError branch, classify load() outcomes three ways -- FileNotFoundError keeps the existing continue/retry; (ValueError, TypeError) (empty file, torn JSON, JSON list, extra-key TypeError from from_dict) enters a bounded fresh-publication re-read sub-loop (100 x 0.005s = ~500ms ceiling, _FRESH_PUBLISH_MAX_REREADS/_FRESH_PUBLISH_REREAD_DELAY_S documented next to _ACQUIRE_MAX_ATTEMPTS) that recovers if the winner finishes publishing, continues the outer O_EXCL loop if the file vanishes, and otherwise raises a DISTINCT RuntimeError 'writer.lock at {path} exists but is not readable JSON; refusing to acquire or delete it' (RuntimeError -> mp worker 'blocked', deliberately NOT containing 'Writer lock held by', and the file is NEVER unlinked in this state); a successful load falls through to the unchanged live->held / not-live->unlink+retry path. load(), from_dict(), save(), release(), heartbeat(), _assert_still_current(), is_live/is_malformed/_parse_iso, the acquire() signature, SCHEMA_VERSION, O_EXCL flags, and _ACQUIRE_MAX_ATTEMPTS are all untouched.

issues.description: Independently discovered and numerically demonstrated by docs/verify-o3-tile-frame-fullgrid-cook-20260929 (2026-09-29), not by O3 itself. O3's own seam check (tools/tile_frame_consistency.py) is weaker than a real geometric seam check: it compares each tile's raw, independently-OSM2World-auto-centered local bounding box against its neighbor's, never applying any tile-placement transform, and its per-pair 'status' field is dead code (always 'INCOMPLETE', never gates the top-level PASS/FAIL). The verifying subagent instead built a ground-truth-anchored check: for 4 adjacent tile pairs from the current-pin full-grid cook (reports/production_readiness/20260924T100614Z_FULL_GRID_TILE_FBX_COOK/), it computed each named OSM building's true lat/lon centroid, projected it into the pipeline's native frame, subtracted the registry rebase offset, matched it to its OSM2World-exported mesh object by name (discovering and correcting for OSM2World's OBJ south-positive Z axis via two independent building-pair distance cross-checks, 1.4% agreement), and computed the per-tile median residual offset needed on top of the only tile-placement convention this codebase documents (tx*1000, ty*1000).
issues.proof: Both north-south adjacent pairs showed a statistically overwhelming, non-noise offset inconsistency: tile_8_8 vs tile_8_9 (y/north-south) delta=176.5m, standard error ~13.9m (~12.7 sigma); tile_7_8 vs tile_7_9 (y/north-south) delta=270.1m, standard error ~21.5m (~12.6 sigma). The production_candidate profile sets allows_waived: true with no classifier, so a waiver could in principle be attached to an identity/integrity gate such as map_registry_identity, converting a genuine integrity defect into a passing release -- per the V5 branch's own audit.

The new V5 fail-closed gates (D16/D17/E24) are therefore structurally unable to consult a waiver at all, which independently confirms the V5 branch's own mitigating-fact claim, but the underlying waiver-model classification gap for gates that DO go through the contract (none of which currently has an executing consumer, per GAP-036) remains unaddressed.
issues.scientific_runtime_consequence: If and when an executing consumer of PRODUCTION_MAP_QUALITY_CONTRACT.yaml is ever built (see GAP-036), the waiver model as it exists today would let a production_candidate-profile release waive an identity/integrity gate (wrong artifact identity, hash mismatch, wrong repository SHA, manifest tampering) using the same mechanism intended for genuine quality-only deviations. V5's own new gates are unaffected today only because they never consult the waiver system at all.
